title: I Let the Archery-Range Lane Timer Hit the Coach Who Wrote It

parts.text: I checked into lane 4 at 6:02 p.m. and the buzzer the coach laminated said: TWENTY MINUTES. NEXT ARROW AFTER THE BEEP. Coach Rhea kept her quiver on 4 past the beep and waved me to the waiting tape. I was twenty-nine, night league, holding a reservation slip with her initials. "Coaches are lanes of safety," she said. I photographed the timer, the slip, and her nocked arrow after the tone. Then I logged a lane-overstay note. At 6:24 the range manager asked why Rhea's name was on a timer ticket. I waited where the camera already was.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The range manager can see Rhea's nocked arrow after the beep on her own timer.

social.video_title: She kept the lane after the beep she laminated — Part 1/2
social.description: Archery, a coach's quiver, and a twenty-minute buzzer she wrote. I logged the overstay. Would you have waited at the tape?

parts.text: Rhea called it a demo until the next shooter asked for the log. I printed the ticket, the photo, and the slip. Safety recoded the buzzer. Rhea shot from the waiting tape and told juniors the timer was always about optics. Optics is a word coaches use when a tone exists. Lane policy now has a second line: COACHES ARE NOT LANES. I keep my twenty. Rhea queues. The range finally sounds like a beep, not a lecture. I go back to being a person with a receipt. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.

social.description: Timer ticket, recoded buzzer, and a second line. Was a demo ever an extra twenty?
